Does bluing come off red like normal rust? Or am I okay in using a little flitz?
A question about rust and bluing
The flitz is an abrasive. You are removing metal by using it. The rust needs off, and a re-blue unless you're worried about destroying the value of an antique weapon.

CLP or Hoppes #9 and a stiff toothbrush and get to scrubbing. You don't want to get creative with solvents that remove the protective coat. You don't want to use scratch pads... unless the finish is already fucked in which case do whatever, it's just a Taurus. Selling it would only get about $350 USD in fair to good condition- less if it's got notable flaws.

In my experience, the best way to remove rust from bluing is with some fine (0000) steel wool and a little oil. Go slow and the bluing won't be harmed. Clean the dirty oil away as you go, it can form an abrasive paste.

Other folks suggest using brass or bronze wool instead. I think any of them are fine.

When the rust is removed you may have some pitting or discoloration left behind. You can just leave it be (I do) or have the gun refinished, but that can get expensive.
